statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. The Nasdaq-100 is holding its session high into the closing hour in an orderly, low-volatility advance; Tail remains below the block threshold.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. An unbroken open-to-high path argues against treating intraday dips as fully reliable mean-reversion points, while VIX at its 14.19 daily low and a 0.75% session range keep Tail well under the blocking band. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the remainder of the power hour and the 20:00Z cash close, where late-session continuation is the nearest amplifier. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: NDX pinned to its session high into the close; low-amplitude trend keeps Tail in the watch band
body: At the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 is near 30,724, up about 0.79%, trading within two points of its 30,725.56 session high after opening at the 30,496.43 session low; NQ futures at 31,011.75 (+0.74%) sit within three points of their own 31,014.25 session high. That unbroken open-to-high path, now holding into the final half hour of cash trading, is the clearest current Tail input and is genuine directional efficiency rather than inference. Its amplitude, however, remains small: the session range is roughly 0.75% and VIX is at 14.21, down 4.44% and printing its 14.19 daily low, so realised volatility is compressing as the trend extends rather than expanding alongside it. Cross-asset inputs are supportive rather than discontinuous and are not broadly aligned. WTI is near $90.08 (-2.48%) and Brent near $98.98 (-1.35%), a fifth consecutive session of declines after a senior Iranian official indicated the Strait of Hormuz could reopen within seven days if US military pressure eases, and with Saudi Arabia restarting its East-West pipeline; that is a de-escalating geopolitical input, which lowers rather than raises path risk. The 10-year note yield is 4.968%, up half a basis point and mid-range on the day, and the 2-year is near 4.76% after today's auction stopped at 4.787%, both consistent with last week's quarter-point Federal Reserve rate increase. Breadth conflicts with the index move: the Dow is down about 0.24% while the Nasdaq-100 is up 0.79%, and shared delayed context shows all seven tracked semiconductors higher with a mean gain near 1.74% while the eight tracked megacaps are split four up and four down. Leadership is therefore narrow and chip-led, following Meta's Muse AI app reaching the top of the App Store. Conflicting breadth of this kind reduces directional conviction and lifts Stress more than it lifts Tail. Offsetting the calm tape, Richmond Fed President Barkin said supply shocks are not proving short-lived and left the door open to further rate increases, the Richmond Fed manufacturing index printed -2 against a forecast of 3, and the national average diesel price reached a record $6.52 with the administration floating an export ban. The combination of a hiking central bank, a 10-year near 5%, a live supply-side inflation impulse and record index levels is a genuinely two-sided, higher-stress backdrop, but the observed price path today is an orderly low-volatility grind rather than a violent no-retracement repricing. Tail is therefore set at 21, reflecting session-extreme holding and observed directional efficiency, while remaining clearly below the blocking band. The next scheduled catalysts are the remainder of the power hour and the 20:00Z cash close today, then the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45Z on 23 September, fifteen minutes after the cash open.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hours carry a published Claude assessment. The 21 September US afternoon peaked at Tail 33 with a trend-up mode and unwound sharply into that cash close, to 23 and then 14. The overnight and European hours of 22 September were consistently quiet, with Tail between 11 and 13 and a normal mode for thirteen straight hours. Tail lifted to 21 at the 22 September cash open, eased back to 17, 15 and 14 through the US morning as the mode was assessed as mixed, then returned to 20 and a trend-up mode in the 18:00Z hour as the index settled near its session high.
outlookSummary: The near-term path is shaped by the remainder of the power hour and the 20:00Z cash close, where continuation of the observed open-to-high drift is the nearest conditional amplifier and Tail is carried at 21 and 20. Conditional Tail then decays through the post-close and overnight hours to 11-13 as cash liquidity leaves and no scheduled catalyst is in force, with mean reversion the base case across the Asian session. Risk rebuilds gradually through the European morning to 14-15, conditional on yields, since the 10-year at 4.968% and last week's rate increase leave the rate-sensitive, chip-led leadership exposed. The clear peak of the forecast is the 13:00Z window on 23 September, where the US cash open at 13:30Z overlaps the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45Z; that slot is carried at Tail 22 in an event/whipsaw mode as a two-way catalyst checkpoint, not as an assumed directional break, and the following hour is held at 21 for delayed second-leg risk around the 14:05Z Fed Barr speech. Conditional Tail then eases to 18-19 through the rest of the US session, with the 5-year note auction at 17:00Z a further yield checkpoint. No forecast hour reaches the blocking band.
